beats.say: Your pipeline is slow. But the cause is inside the database.
beats.text: The cause is in the database

beats.say: Why does change capture lag? Why does a replica return old rows?
beats.label: Interview questions
beats.head: Why is the replica stale?

beats.say: Three ideas answer most of them: the storage engine, transactions, and replication.
beats.label: Track 2 · Database foundations

check.prompt: A store takes very heavy writes all day. Which engine fits?
check.why: An LSM-tree only appends, so writes are very fast. It merges files later.

beats.say: First: how does a database store rows?
A B-tree keeps data sorted in pages. Reads are fast. Each write updates a page in place.
beats.label: B-tree
beats.head: Sorted pages, fast reads

beats.say: An LSM-tree only appends. Writes are very fast. Later, it merges files in the background.
beats.label: LSM-tree
beats.head: Append now, merge later

beats.say: So: many reads, pick a B-tree. Very heavy writes, pick an LSM-tree.
beats.label: The choice
beats.head: Reads: B-tree. Writes: LSM-tree.

check.prompt: Why does log-based CDC put little load on the tables?
check.why: The database writes every change to the log first. CDC reads that log, not the tables.

beats.say: Second: how does a database stay correct?
Before it changes any data, the database writes the change to a log.
beats.label: Write-ahead log
beats.head: Log first, data second

beats.say: After a crash, it replays the log. Nothing that was committed is lost.
beats.label: After a crash
beats.head: Replay the log

beats.say: Change data capture reads that same log. That is why CDC does not load the tables.
beats.label: For pipelines
beats.head: CDC reads the log

beats.say: Third: copies of the data, on other machines.
A leader takes the writes. Replicas copy them, a little later.
beats.label: Single leader
beats.head: Replicas are a little behind

beats.say: So a read from a replica can be stale. This is called replication lag.
beats.label: The trap
beats.head: Replication lag

beats.say: And when the network splits, you must choose: stay consistent, or stay available.
beats.label: CAP
beats.head: Consistent or available

beats.say: Last: read from a source without hurting it.
A full dump is simple but heavy. An updated-at filter misses deletes. Log-based CDC sees everything.
beats.label: Three ways to extract

beats.say: Quick recap of database foundations.
B-tree for reads, LSM for writes. The log comes first. And replicas lag.
beats.label: Database foundations

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
